newsitem.title: USA: Tosco to buy 76 Products from Unocal for $1.4 billion.
newsitem.headline: Tosco to buy 76 Products from Unocal for $1.4 billion.

text.p: Tosco Corp. signed a letter of intent to purchase 76 Products Co., the West Coast refining, marketing and transportation division of Unocal Corp., for between $1.9 billion and $2.1 billion, the companies said Monday.
The price includes $1.4 billion for 76 Products' fixed assets, about $400 million for inventories and up to $250 million in future profits if gasoline margins rise in the next seven years, they said.

"This acquisition makes Tosco the largest independent refiner and marketer in the United States, with over 950,000 barrels per day of refining capacity and 12 million gallons per day of retail fuel sales," said Thomas D. O'Malley, Tosco's chairman and chief executive officer.
"On the retail side, the 76 retail system, added to Tosco's existing California properties, makes Tosco the third-largest retailer in the state of California."
Costa Mesa, Calif.-based 76 Products also has retail outlets and terminals in Hawaii, which will provide a new market for Tosco, which operates Circle K convenience stores.

The acquisition includes Unocal's California refining system, with a throughput capacity of 250,000 barrels per day, and a retail system that sells over 100,000 barrels per day of gasoline and diesel fuel.

The retail system consists of about 1,350 76-branded gasoline stations, 1,100 of which are company-controlled. Tosco will acquire the 76 brand in the refining and marketing business on a worldwide basis.

The deal also includes a distribution system comprised of 13 company-owned oil storage terminals, three modern tankers and 1,500 miles of crude oil and product pipeline. Tosco will also take over the worldwide assets of Unocal's extensive lubricants manufacturing, distribution and marketing business.
Tosco will assume limited environmental liabilities.
The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 1997, subject to approval by both companies' boards, Tosco shareholders and regulators.
Stamford, Conn.-based Tosco said the merger will generate substantial selling, general and administrative cost savings.

Tosco will fund the acquisition with a combination of debt and equity. "Given the current earnings power of the Unocal assets, the equity issue should be accretive to per-share earnings," O'Malley said.
Unocal said the sale is part of the company's long-term strategy to grow by pursuing large projects in Asia.

"With this sale, we can focus on expanding our role as a major international energy producer and project developer and on strengthening our domestic U.S. oil and gas operations in the Louisiana/Gulf of Mexico region," said Roger C. Beach, Unocal's chairman and chief executive.
He said the company's diversified business group, which includes agricultural products, Molycorp, UNO-VEN and other businesses, will remain an important part of Unocal's operations.
El Segundo, Calif.-based Unocal said it expects to record a $375 million after-tax book loss from the sale.

Tosco, with more than $11 billion in annual revenues, is one of the nation's largest independent refiners and marketers of petroleum products, and is the nation's largest operator of company-controlled convenience stores.
Neither company's stock immediately began trading when the markets opened Monday. Unocal's stock closed Friday at $39.50 and Tosco closed at $60.125, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
